name: Revenue recognition — rendering of services
definition: Revenue from a service transaction is recognised as the service is performed, measured either by the proportionate completion method or by the completed service contract method, whichever relates the revenue to the work accomplished, and only when no significant uncertainty exists about the amount of the consideration.
why_it_exists: A service is consumed over time, so there is no single moment of delivery to anchor recognition to. AS-9 replaces that missing moment with a measure of performance. Without it, an enterprise could book a twelve-month contract on day one or on the last day, and both would look defensible.
inputs: the contract and what it requires the enterprise to do
whether performance is one act or more than one act
degree of completion evidence: contract value, associated costs, number of acts, or other suitable basis
outputs: the recognition method: proportionate completion or completed service contract
revenue recognised for the period, or postponed
preconditions: a service transaction, not a sale of goods
the transaction is not one of the AS-9 scope exclusions (see ACC-REV-SCOPE-EXCLUSIONS)
exceptions: AS 9 does not deal with revenue from construction contracts, hire-purchase and lease agreements, government grants and other similar subsidies, or insurance contracts of insurance companies — see ACC-REV-SCOPE-EXCLUSIONS
common_mistakes: recognising the whole contract value on signing, when performance consists of more than one act

using straight line spreading where the acts are determinate and countable — AS 9 permits straight line only for an indeterminate number of acts over a specific period, and only where no other method better represents the pattern of performance
recognising on the final act when performance actually consists of many acts, which defers revenue that was already earned
treating the completed service contract method as a free choice — AS 9 ties the method to the pattern of performance
legal_references: UNKNOWN — statutory backing not extracted from any downloaded source in this pass
gst_references: NOT APPLICABLE — GST time of supply for services is a separate determination and must not be conflated with accounting revenue recognition
evidence_required: the service contract or its terms
evidence of what has been performed to date
the basis used to measure completion: contract value, associated costs, number of acts, or other stated basis
confidence_factors: weak when the document does not show whether performance is one act or many
weak when no measurable basis of completion appears in the document
weak when the contract period is not stated, because straight line spreading then has no period to spread over
validation_checks: the method chosen matches the stated pattern of performance, not the convenience of the period
revenue recognised does not exceed the proportion of performance evidenced
no significant uncertainty exists regarding the amount of the consideration, or recognition is postponed
examples: annual maintenance contract, twelve monthly visits of equal scope, no other pattern evidenced — proportionate completion, straight line over the period
a single valuation report delivered and chargeable on delivery — completed service contract method, recognised when the final act takes place
counterexamples: a construction contract — excluded from AS 9 by paragraph 2(i), so this concept does not decide it
advance fee received before any act is performed — receipt is not performance, so nothing is recognised on receipt alone

evidence.quote: recognised as the service is performed, either by the proportionate completion method or by the completed service contract method

In a transaction involving the rendering of services, performance should be measured either under the completed service contract method or under the proportionate completion method, whichever relates the revenue to the work accomplished.
Such performance should be regarded as being achieved when no significant uncertainty exists regarding the amount of the consideration that will be derived from rendering the service.
